sections.h2: Which office handles property tax for a house in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
Real estate valuation, billing and payment all run through the county Tax Department at 230 Government Center Drive in Wilmington. Its phone line is (910) 798-7300, and the reappraisal team answers by email at reappraisal@nhcgov.com.

The county explains that your bill comes from two ingredients: your property's assessed value and a rate per $100 that elected county and municipal boards adopt. Those boards usually settle the rate in June. Assessed value in New Hanover County is set at 100% of estimated market value as of the last revaluation.

sections.h2: What do New Hanover County and its beach towns charge per $100?
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2026-2027 the county rate is 30.6 cents per $100. Where a house sits decides what else lands on the bill, since Wilmington and three beach towns add their own rates.

Rates for fiscal year 2026-2027 listed in the New Hanover County Tax Department's July 2026 bill release

Source: New Hanover County Tax Department release. Owners outside municipal limits also see a stormwater services fee as its own line on the bill.

sections.h2: What is the payment calendar for New Hanover County bills?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed ahead of a September 1 due date. The county accepts payment without interest through January 5. G.S. 105-360 sets the interest steps after that: 2% through the end of January, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of a month.

The county splits each bill into four equal coupons so a household can pay in pieces. Ways to pay named in its release:

  • Card or e-check at the Tax Office counter.
  • InvoiceCloud online, which carries a service fee, or 1-877-309-0878 by phone.
  • The outdoor drop box to the right of the Government Center's main door.
  • Check by mail to PO Box 18000, Wilmington, NC 28406.

Escrowed owners get a courtesy notice and should confirm their lender paid. Anyone who may run past January 5 is urged to call before January 6 and ask about a payment plan.

sections.h2: When does New Hanover County revalue homes?
sections.html:
On a four-year cycle. State law only demands a reappraisal every eight years, but commissioners voted in 2008 to go to four, and the first four-year revaluation took effect January 1, 2012. The present values date from January 1, 2025, and the next is scheduled for January 1, 2029.

For analysis the county sorts roughly 115,000 parcels into about 1,500 neighborhoods. Appraisers study home and land sales, make field and desk reviews, and use aerial imagery and computer models, then publish a Schedule of Values that the commissioners must approve. Between revaluations, a value moves only for things like new construction, damage, errors in the record or a change in use, and market swings wait for the next cycle.

A house still being built on January 1 is taxed at whatever stage it has reached, then at full value the following year. Real property stays permanently listed, but new improvements must be listed in January, and the Tax Department will help an owner list them.

sections.h2: How do you contest a value in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
Use the county's appeal form, which costs nothing and needs no lawyer. Appeals open the day the value notice arrives and close when the board adjourns. For tax year 2026 the cutoff was 5:00 pm on May 14, 2026, so that window has shut. The county nudges owners to file within 30 days of the notice so staff can review before the Board of Equalization and Review.

The burden of proof is on the owner. Helpful evidence, per the county, includes:

  • Sales of comparable homes that closed before January 1, 2025.
  • Photos showing condition or defects.
  • Notes on improvements the record gets wrong.
  • A formal appraisal dated before January 1, 2025, which is optional.

A dispute that survives informal review goes to the Board of Equalization and Review, which the county describes as local residents drawn from brokerage, appraisal, construction and law, sitting in smaller panels. Owners may appear or send papers instead. The board meets in the April to early May window, and its written ruling follows within 30 days. Beyond it lies the state Property Tax Commission, reachable under G.S. 105-290.

Any joint owner can file for the group. A business owner may send an officer, manager, W-2 employee or 25% owner. Other non-attorney helpers are limited to hardship cases such as illness, a death in the family or military deployment. Commercial owners are asked for three years of income and expense statements and a rent roll dated before January 1, 2025.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can lower a New Hanover County bill?
sections.html:
Seniors, veterans and disabled owners have three state programs to ask about, and the county's FAQ lists all of them. Only one can apply to a given owner, and the paperwork is Form AV-9, filed with the assessor.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: protects the larger of $25,000 or half the value; $38,800 is the 2026 income ceiling.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: protects $45,000 of value, and the form states there is no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the bill at 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for incomes up to $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home.

File in January if you can, though forms are accepted through June 1 before the tax year. Circuit breaker enrollees reapply yearly, and taxes above the cap are put off rather than waived, so a sale brings back the preceding three years.

sections.h2: What if taxes are unpaid when a New Hanover County house sells?
sections.html:
The obligation stays attached to the parcel, per G.S. 105-355. Ask the Tax Department at (910) 798-7300 for a payoff figure and pass it to the person handling your closing.

Left unpaid, the lien can be foreclosed through the courts under G.S. 105-374. A seller who clears the balance with the sale avoids that route.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for New Hanover County?
sections.html:
New Hanover County's 2025 population estimate is 245,959, which is 9.0% above the April 2020 base. The land area is 192.26 square miles, and 2020 density was 1,174.0 people per square mile. The typical owner-occupied house carried a $387,800 value in the 2020 to 2024 survey period, and owners paid a median $1,888 monthly with a mortgage or $658 without one.

Median household income was $75,166. Residents past 65 make up 21.3% of the county, a group the exclusions above are designed for. With 2,332 permits issued in 2025, plenty of owners have new improvements to list.

faqs.q: What day are New Hanover County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. The county allows payment without interest through January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6.

faqs.q: How much is the New Hanover County tax rate?
faqs.a: Thirty and six-tenths cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-2027, with 7.25 cents more for fire services in unincorporated areas. Municipal rates are added inside Wilmington and the beach towns.

faqs.q: When is the next New Hanover County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2029, according to the county. The current values took effect January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to appeal a New Hanover County assessment?
faqs.a: No, and an attorney is not required. Evidence should be dated before January 1, 2025 for the current values.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid taxes when a New Hanover County house sells?
faqs.a: They remain a lien on the parcel. Get a payoff amount from the Tax Department and have the closing attorney clear it.
